To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the following volatile metal species have been identified in the urban atmosphere of Bordeaux (France): tetraethyl lead, tetramethyl lead, trimethyl lead, dimethyl selenoide, elemental mercury, dimethyl tin and trimethyl tin.

(1) the atmospheric concentration of volatile metal species is highly dependent on their source, (2) the atmospheric concentration is highly dependent on meteorological conditions, (3) the concentration of volatile metal compounds in urban atmosphere is highly dependent on traffic intensity, and (4) the occurrence of unknown volatile metal species likely to occur is a major issue.

1) The main volatile metal species in urban atmosphere are elemental mercury, tetraalkyllead species and dimethyl selenone; 2) Volatile metal species concentrations are highly variable depending on meteorological conditions and the site location.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new methods for the analysis of trace metals and their species in the environment.
the development of new analytical techniques to measure and speciate volatile metal and metalloids in air and to study their distribution in different urban environment.
the development of novel, highly selective, efficient, and cost-effective catalysts for the synthesis of organic compounds.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the present work is the first study of volatile metals and metalloids in a European urban area, and that the results show the potentialities of the analytical method used for this type of study.
the present study is an important contribution to the knowledge of volatile metal and organometallic compounds in urban atmosphere.

- the atmospheric concentrations of volatile lead species have dropped dramatically in the last decade, - the concentrations of other volatile metal and metaloid species (Hg, Se) are still significant and need further investigation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that there are many volatile species that can be measured in urban air.
we have developed a method for the determination of volatile metal and selenium compounds in air, which is suitable for routine measurements.

the use of a cryogenic trap for the sampling and the use of a low-temperature gas-chromatograph for the separation of metal and metalloid volatile compounds, associated with a ICP-MS for the detection of the species of interest, has allowed the detection and quantification of volatile metal and volatile metalloid species (Hg, Pb, Se) in an European urban atmosphere (the city of Bordeaux).
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of volatile metal species in the urban atmosphere can be explained in a large part by the presence of anthropogenic sources.
the atmospheric mercury cycle is not only driven by anthropogenic emissions, but that natural sources of Hg can also be significant.
there are still some unknown volatile metal species that may occur in urban environment.
